editorial:
Ever wonder how those cool, stylish crime movies from the sixties actually happened? You get a front-row seat to the chaos behind the scenes of the 1967 classic Point Blank. This documentary introduces you to director Alan Berry as he digs into the wild partnership between the tough-as-nails Lee Marvin and the visionary John Boorman. You will feel like you are hanging out with the crew, hearing stories about the fights, the weird filming choices, and the overall mood of a set where everyone was trying to push the limits of what a movie could look like.

What really hits home is how the film shows the grit and hard work that went into every shot. The pacing is steady, and the real-life stories are often more exciting than the movie itself. While it might be a bit slow for people who hate talking-head docs, it is a goldmine for film buffs. You should definitely try to find this in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video to see those old clips in the best quality possible. If you prefer owning your movies, adding the 4K Blu-ray to your physical collection is the way to go for the best experience.
endingExplained: The documentary wraps up by showing how the movie changed the way action films were made forever. It ends by looking at the legacy of Lee Marvin's performance and how John Boorman's style influenced later directors. You see the final results of the editing process and learn how the movie became a hit despite the struggles during filming. It finishes on a high note, celebrating the art of the crime thriller.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves old crime movies and learning how films are made.
